campaign.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
campaign.objective: Introduce Aurelia and its business software through press and television advertising, NCC presentations, a ComputerLand sales premiere and the public launch of Logix Computer Academy.
message: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
Learn before you decide.
Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia through newspaper and business-press teasers, then invite customers and press to the premiere.

marketing_presentation.description: Begin newspaper and business-press teasers on {start_date}, introducing Aurelia as a personal assistant in business. Start with “coming this spring”, then publish the {premiere_date} premiere date and invite brochure and presentation-invitation requests.

Follow the teasers with explanatory print advertisements about Aurelia, Abacus and independently branded BPI applications. Prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage, so readers can act on the campaign through local demonstrations and training enquiries.

During late May and early June, organise joint Logix/BPI press previews, prepare dealers and demonstration staff, issue launch invitations and rehearse the Aurelia presentation. Staff telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demonstration appointments and Academy bookings.

marketing_steps.description: Run the cinematic Aurelia television commercial and direct viewers to demonstrations.

marketing_presentation.description: The proposed advertisement is a {duration_seconds}-second film trailer, with {lead} proposed as its lead. In the final {reveal_seconds} seconds, show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, the logo and the June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable, independently branded BPI report; explain accounting in the accompanying press campaign and follow-up films. Casting remains subject to contract.

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration. Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence. Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia as a business assistant at NCC on 5 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Present on the {stage}, using {projector_count} video projectors. Record the full presentation and make it available to television broadcasters under {rebroadcast_terms}.
Open with the {computer} television commercial.

{presenter} describes {development_period} of work to bring {computer} to market. Early cars used tillers, levers, rotary cranks and cross-shaped handles before the steering wheel became the familiar standard. Personal computers reached an important milestone in {assembled_computer_year}: buyers no longer had to assemble them. Yet their controls still resemble those early experiments—awkward, inconsistent and hard to learn. He introduces Aurelia as a computer with a steering wheel: a consistent, intuitive way to work.

{presenter} reveals {computer_count} Aurelia computers. A camera circles them, showing every angle on the projection screens. Then show {commercial_count} new commercials: a housewife prints recipes, a schoolboy uses the on-screen calculator, and a businessman checks his diary of meetings and tasks.

{presenter} switches on {computer} and opens the {tools} menu. He loads a text document from disk, demonstrates editing, cursor navigation and selection, and copies and pastes text. He then finds a contact in the directory and pastes its details into the document, showing how familiar actions carry across applications.
{presenter} connects a printer while the computer remains on and prints the document. He demonstrates the calculator and a calendar of tasks and events, then prints the next day’s schedule.

{presenter} connects another disk drive and loads {spreadsheet} from disk. He explains its rules and calculations, then opens a large, complex accounting sheet. Changing one input immediately updates calculations throughout the sheet; he prints the result. He asks, “How many commands did I have to memorise?” to underline that the audience has followed familiar actions rather than memorised instructions.

{presenter} invites {os_speaker} from {os_company}, {logix_speaker} from {computer_company}, {software_speaker} from {software_company}, and a representative of {retailer} onto the stage. He introduces the {platform_bits}-bit platform, with its specifications displayed on the screens.

{speaker} explains that Aurelia runs applications for {compatible_version} and introduces {new_version} with a text user interface. The operating system belongs to {owner} and is available to other manufacturers whose hardware meets its requirements. He thanks {partner} for supporting this approach.
{speaker} presents Aurelia pricing and the {support_levels}-level support system, including telephone help through a call centre.

{speaker} introduces the {ide} and announces its presentation on {developer_session}. He explains that {software_company} and {application_company} have ported their applications to C and the new user interface; the business applications will be demonstrated on {business_session}.
The {retailer} representative announces product availability in its shops from {retail_date}. {speaker} introduces {academy}, opening on {academy_date}, and the try-before-you-buy programme.

{presenter} explains {company}’s plans for expansion cards, FlexiBUS devices and monitors: limited further in-house development, with third-party products welcomed. Products meeting the compatibility criteria can receive {certification} under {certification_terms}. He invites everyone to try Aurelia at the booth.

Close with questions and answers. Keep reminders on screen for the C development session ({developer_session}), BPI presentation ({business_session}), ComputerLand sales premiere ({retail_date}) and Logix Academy launch ({academy_date}).

marketing_steps.description: Present AION C IDE and the Software Developer Package on the morning of 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Introduce the platform interfaces that the Software Developer Package exposes: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation and licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development. Explain how those interfaces support application and peripheral work on Aurelia.

Use {ide} with {sdk} to edit a small application with syntax highlighting and diagnostic navigation. Build it using a qualified optimization profile, link an assembly library and debug the application in RAM. Explain C source portability and the need for separate target builds rather than promising universal binary compatibility.

Demonstrate keyboard-operated TUI forms with bounded data controls and calls into the shared ROM TUI. Show text and bitmap presentation in tested modes, distinguishing SDK composite helpers from native ROM services. Publish measured memory, disk and performance results; shared source and API contracts do not imply that future targets have already been released.

marketing_steps.description: Present the independent BPI business applications on the afternoon of 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in this dedicated session.
{provider} covers setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage.

Use pilot demonstrations with {pilot_businesses} businesses and several accounting practices to prepare representative BPI workflows. Reconcile their results against existing records, checking data volumes, disk and RAM requirements, posting, corrections, backup and restore, payroll jurisdiction coverage and the summary export to Abacus. Publish measured capacity and supported configurations without treating pilot targets as completed results.

marketing_steps.description: Hold the official Aurelia sales premiere at a ComputerLand shop on 14 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: {dealer} hosts the official Aurelia sales premiere with {logix}. Introduce the retail offering, demonstrate the business-assistant workflow and help visitors choose a suitable system and associated software. Keep separately licensed BPI applications and training distinct from the computer purchase.

marketing_steps.description: Officially launch Logix Computer Academy and its BPI programme on 16 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: The Academy was established on {established_date} and is announced publicly on {announcement_date}. Officially launch on {launch_date} with an initial {city_count}-city US programme with a {fundamentals_days}-day Fundamentals course. Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases. Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.

The {launch_date} Academy launch includes BPI-authorised practical courses and direct distribution, dealer qualification, accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist. Dealers handle first-line installation enquiries, BPI handles software defects and specialist support, and Logix supports hardware. Training, setup services and software licences remain separate offerings. Train instructors and dealers to explain advertised modules, published requirements and support boundaries.

marketing_steps.description: Record the NCC presentations and distribute cleared television coverage.

marketing_presentation.description: Before NCC, contact television stations and arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights for redistribution. Include Michael Douglas commercial footage only if it is separately cleared for that use.

Throughout 5–8 June 1978, use a professional multi-camera crew to record every Logix NCC presentation and hands-on demonstration, including the premiere, technical and developer content, partner appearances, additional sessions and questions. Capture clean presenter audio, audience reactions and close-ups of the computer, display, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

Preserve demonstration fidelity: do not accelerate startup or recalculation, hide failures with misleading cuts or present recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and any recorded fallback.

After NCC, prepare a business-user broadcast feature, short station-ready news and demonstration excerpts, clean captioned footage, separate narration or audio where practical, a factual product and Academy press sheet, and full edited presentations for longer technical coverage. Offer cleared, Logix-identified material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication, dispatch and station-compatible copies. Distribution follows editing and clearance. Stations choose their own participation, schedules and editorial selection; no airtime or endorsement is guaranteed.

marketing_steps.description: Plan year-end workshops and customer-led expansion after the launch.

marketing_presentation.description: Prepare year-end workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations, specifying payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Keep customer data under customer control and obtain consent before presenting referrals as accountant endorsements. This is follow-up planning, not a claim that year-end work is complete within the campaign period.

Plan expansion of demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results, explaining the module-to-suite upgrade route. BPI support for the Model II remains a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.

campaign.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
campaign.objective: Encourage independent manufacturers and developers to adopt documented compatibility interfaces, and show customers how supported software, documents and peripherals can protect their investment across computer brands.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Use documented interfaces and qualified configurations to connect products from independent suppliers.
Choose CP/M applications, FlexiBUS peripherals and display options separately; adopting one does not require the entire Logix platform.
Prepare for future computers through portable C source and documented interfaces while continuing to use and support established eight-bit systems.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify partner claims and protect the next-generation architecture disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not change software ownership or imply open-source licensing. Reference-code rights, certification scope and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.
Claim compatibility only for named software versions, resources, host adapters and tested configurations. Preserve each supplier’s brand, licences and support responsibilities.
Label the Model II demonstration as a prototype until customer release. AION supplies the June 1979 cards; SMC remains a future source subject to individual chip qualification.

Apple’s demonstration participation covers native Apple II products and does not endorse S-100 systems. These products provide neither Apple CP/M/Z80 execution nor automatic conversion of existing Apple graphics.

Until 19 May 1980, refer to future systems only as next-generation computers. Withhold product, processor and OS names; word size, ISA, registers, execution design, address and memory organisation; performance figures, clock rates, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology and future display specifications.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, future-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.
Do not imply an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

marketing_steps.description: Demonstrate independent customer choices at NCC 1979.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Explain how independent software, peripheral and display choices can protect a customer’s investment.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the Model II prototype using separately qualified host editions. Show supported common behaviour without promising identical binaries or disk formats.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate Abacus, then independent BPI records and summary export. Explain the prepared data and separate licensing; do not imply that BPI has a Model II port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, driver support and supported application functions, attaching only when the port is quiescent.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Present the Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II alongside the S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. An Apple representative joins the native Apple demonstration. Explain the drivers, optional display hardware and separate S-100 support without suggesting Apple endorses S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, BPI management and confirmed peripheral participants explain their responsibilities and commercial access. Distinguish current AION chip supply from prospective SMC supply and signed partners from recruitment prospects.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter} explains that future computers will not run existing Z80 binaries natively. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration work; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. Describe the planned optional Z80 coprocessor and the continuing role of eight-bit systems without revealing the new architecture.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Identify available products, prototypes and future plans. Direct customers and developers to documented configurations, licence terms, the compatibility directory and programme registration.

marketing_steps.description: Explain the separate software, peripheral and display compatibility profiles.

marketing_presentation.description: Specify the CP/M core and optional extension versions, processor instruction set, available transient-program memory, adapters and qualified applications for each configuration. Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit.
Explain implementation and qualification requirements for {subject}.
Explain supported interaction behaviour under {subject}.
Present {subject} to developers implementing supported interfaces.
Explain source portability through {subject}, with recompilation and testing still required.
Distinguish graphics API compatibility under {subject} from qualified display hardware.
Explain the qualified monitor connection defined by {subject}; this is not a consumer television interface.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent implementers under explicit terms and governance.

marketing_presentation.description: Describe DRI’s software leadership and Logix’s hardware contribution. Invite independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers to a programme offering published specifications, versioning, backward-support policies, reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. Explain non-exclusive own-brand implementation, equal access to qualified components, disclosed supply priorities and manufacturer representation in a working group.

Identify the unresolved licence terms, reference-code redistribution rights, support duration and staffing, legacy-maintenance budget, working-group charter and voting rules, certification operator and scope, supply allocations, lead times and warranties. Present these as matters to settle, not existing contractual guarantees.

Invite suppliers to offer wider carriage, letter-quality printing, specialist forms and faster devices. Require the relevant status, character or graphics, paper and form-control support; the basic printer protocol does not cover every feature.
Invite business-chart and engineering-output devices, subject to a new plotting profile and suitable application support.
Invite communications and remote-access products with defined serial data, flow-control, modem-status and control profiles and host drivers.

Invite larger floppy systems, backup products and selected hard disks. Specify geometry, removable-media errors, durable writes, boot rules and measured throughput. Native faster disk controllers remain a valid choice.
Invite instruments, readers and business-input devices with published class or vendor-extension profiles and host drivers. Do not imply that foreign-processor ROM drivers execute automatically.

marketing_steps.description: Explain source migration, legacy support and the continuing eight-bit market.

marketing_presentation.description: The 4 June 1979 announcement explains source migration and the planned optional Z80 compatibility path. Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for 19 May 1980. The all-years technical catalogue is internal author material, not a 1979 press kit.

Use the established Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separate platform adapters. A later target needs recompilation and testing, with review of assembly code, integer and pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access. Source portability does not preserve native Z80 binary execution.

Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television. A computer intended to use an existing television requires separate display engineering; the basic-storage configuration remains unresolved.

marketing_steps.description: Prepare the actual transfer demonstration, venue and architecture answers.

marketing_presentation.description: Document the actual file-transfer route and floppy formats used for the Aurelia-to-Model-II round trip. Publish tested RAM and application-workspace requirements, load and recalculation times and document-capacity limits. Label prepared data and recordings and preserve independent BPI branding and participant clearances.
Use booked presentation space; main-stage access, the exact slot and audiovisual suitability require confirmation. The eight presentation stages total 50 minutes, followed by questions.

Use this response to questions seeking confidential details: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

marketing_steps.description: Evaluate manufacturer adoption against stated targets.

marketing_presentation.description: By the end of 1979, aim for Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified third-party devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, aim for three to five distinct non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations. Count Tandy once and exclude duplicate dealer builds and product variants; these are targets, not achieved results.

campaign.title: Artemis. A new generation. A familiar way to work.
campaign.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Artemis, demonstrate its workflows and explain the compatibility commitment.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter}: the business task and familiar way to work
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. AIONix multitasking: edit, calculate and switch using familiar TUI conventions
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Native Business Tools and Abacus 2 charts/document fields; then independent BPI head demonstrates accounting
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. One maintained C project, separate ERA and Z80 builds; optional compatibility card runs qualified unchanged legacy binaries
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis: verified calculation benchmark, then visible animation
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Reveal: 32-bit RISC ERA 1 developed by AION

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Publish the compatibility commitment through 2000 and its precise scope Announce the compatibility commitment on {announcement_date}, with support through {support_end}. This is a commitment; future fulfilment remains to be demonstrated. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Undocumented hardware access, unqualified peripherals and unsupported interfaces; no promise of unchanged speed, unlimited memory, or every future device. Z80 programs use their separately qualified compatibility path. Publish versioned ABI/API eligibility and conformance tests; preserve reference binaries and regression workloads; budget compatibility engineering, runtime distribution and support. Staffing, funding and validation remain explicit launch readiness gates.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Partners: independent BPI head, Digital Research and qualified device/software partners
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Qualified configurations, order routes, developer kits and training
After the 55-minute presentation

Incremental qualified 80×40 and 80×25 high-resolution text demonstrations, grayscale bitmap/sprites, explicit old-monitor limitations and replaceable card. Retain existing presentation duration; incorporate into Artemis product demonstration.
The independent native business application presented is {subject}; its qualification and support remain separate.

marketing_steps.description: Compare computation and display workloads under reproducible conditions.

marketing_presentation.description: Compare {systems}, using separately measured computation and rendering paths.

Identical vector transformations and fixed-point precision, inputs, rounding and verified output; time computation separately from rendering and I/O. Publish source, compiler options, configuration and repeat-run range.
Same shaded rotating cube, geometry and image quality; identify display hardware, frame-buffer and display-transfer costs separately. Do not infer pure CPU speed from unequal graphics systems.
Publish measured ratios only after reproducible qualification; no forecast assumes an unmeasured speed multiplier.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify application, licensing, resource and support claims before publication.

marketing_presentation.description: Beyond the 64 KB application barrier; demonstrate a measured resident workload on a named 128 KB or 256 KB configuration. Finite RAM and process limits remain; no demand paging promised.

Professional multitasking AIONix with Unix V7-inspired behaviour and familiar Logix TUI/keyboard conventions. Do not claim a Unix source licence or trademark endorsement without an established agreement.

Artemis-hosted AION C IDE supplies ERA native and Z80 cross-compilers, target libraries and separate executables. Portable code following guidelines can require small changes; quantify changes for each demonstration rather than promising zero work.

Native Abacus 2, Business Tools and qualified independent BPI editions. Pulse 1 remains Aurelia+ software; a card demonstration requires guest OS/memory qualification. Native Pulse 3 and Abacus 3 launch only at COMDEX on November 19.
Aurelia+ remains a supported value option; compatible independent 8-bit computers grow the ecosystem. No forced migration or promise that cheaper 8-bit demand disappears.
Measured benchmark and reproducible display comparison
Qualified demo memory/process footprint and printing paths
Published native/card application matrix and OS licensing status
Versioned compatibility policy, engineering owner, staffing and funded maintenance plan
Dealer stock/service readiness and Academy instructor qualification

campaign.title: COMDEX 1979 campaign and presentation
campaign.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
message: More room to work. More freedom to choose.
Your existing software. Less waiting.
Calculate once. Chart it. Print the documents.

marketing_steps.description: Present Aurelia+, Abacus 2 and qualified partner applications at COMDEX 1979.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter}: growing businesses need more capacity, less waiting and compatible choices.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Identical live calculated shaded-cube animation on Aurelia and Aurelia+, followed by identical Abacus recalculation and chart generation; present measured results. Use {explanation_minutes} minute for explanation and {animation_minutes} minutes for the live shaded cube. Calculate rotation, project vertices, determine visible faces, calculate shading and draw a fixed sequence of cube rotations live. No prerecorded animation or precomputed frames. Same executable and inputs on both machines, compatible with both Same resolution, shading method, rendering settings and equivalent qualified display configurations; disclose unavoidable differences Visible start countdown, elapsed time and completed-frame count Fixed frame/rotation sequence completes the same amount of work; no silent frame skipping or quality reduction Use a workload that fits both machines; demonstrate additional capacity separately Both machines must finish correctly; publish results only after measurement Same Abacus 2.0 executable, worksheet values/formulas, calculation settings and chart workload. Compare recalculation and chart-generation time; exclude physical printer time. Animation measures the combined calculation/display path, not pure CPU performance. The catalog clocks are 4 and 6 MHz, but no 1.5x or other application speedup is promised.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Chart employee pay values; link fields to a payslip layout; preview employees and print the entire batch. Demonstrate charts and document layouts populated by spreadsheet field values. Use the catalogued text-mode vertical or horizontal bar charts; do not imply unimplemented graphical chart types. Fictitious employees with names, departments, pay components, deductions and precalculated net pay; one row per employee. Inspect precalculated values and reconcile totals Show a payroll-cost bar chart by department Open one reusable payslip layout and identify linked spreadsheet fields Preview different employees to show field substitution Print one complete payslip per employee from the same layout Validate field mapping, missing values, numeric formatting and rounding Validate pagination and ensure every selected employee prints exactly once with the correct values Validate save/reopen and preserve spreadsheet/document contents Reconcile BPI-exported values with source totals through documented versioned disk-file exchange Abacus charts, formats and prints supplied calculations. Payroll law/rules, statutory deductions and updates belong to the payroll application or properly maintained worksheet. No direct ledger write-back or live database link. Supporting implementation advantage for useful workloads, not a permanently exclusive general technique. Promote Abacus 2.0 on both Aurelia and Aurelia+ in supported configurations. Do not imply a new computer is required.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. The head of independent BPI demonstrates BPI Payroll as the source of calculated values, documented file exchange and reconciled totals.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate a focused information-management task using tested, implemented capabilities; no implied live cross-application integration.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Introduce the Compatibility Kit, reference adapters and diagnostics. Show an independent application implementation only after qualification; otherwise show clearly labelled engineering work.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. BPI leadership joins participating peripheral/computer suppliers. Name products and distinguish shipping, qualified and prototype status.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Purchasing, existing-Aurelia upgrades, ongoing support and independent manufacturer participation; new hardware focus on Aurelia+.
The independent business application presented is {subject}; retain its own branding, licensing and support.

marketing_steps.description: Keep independent supplier roles and qualified configurations explicit.

marketing_presentation.description: Independent branding, management, licences and support. The head of BPI speaks immediately after Abacus and joins the partner segment.
Demonstrate only individually qualified configurations. Invitations and targets are not agreements or shipments.

Published interfaces and kit permit independent Aurelia-class implementations; support and certification optional. Native hardware adapters are valid; FlexiBUS and Logix video are separate profiles. Proper application/OS/firmware licences remain necessary.

marketing_steps.description: Explain upgrades, continued support and independent manufacturer participation.

marketing_presentation.description: Clearly identify the hardware, required software and printing configuration; distinguish BPI licences and specialist setup.
New capabilities for the computer you already own. Publish configuration requirements and explain workloads that benefit from Aurelia+.
Published specifications/self-tests, physical compatibility kits, optional bounded assistance and configuration-specific certification; no exclusive partnership required.
Interoperability sessions and verified directory listings; document production supplies a concrete printer use case.
Promote training, demonstration access and implementation help.
Logix focuses new hardware development and promotion on Aurelia+ while enabling independent Aurelia-class clones and maintaining installed-base support; no immediate withdrawal date.

marketing_steps.description: Explain migration without disclosing the future architecture early.

marketing_presentation.description: Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for {reveal_date}.
Native binary compatibility will change; established C practices reduce migration work; a planned optional Z80 path supports qualified legacy code.
No future product/processor/OS names, word size, architecture, future-target compiler output, binaries or revealing demonstrations before NCC 1980.

campaign.title: A clear view of your next design.
campaign.objective: Generate qualified CAD evaluations and dealer demonstrations for the Artemis/AutoCAD offering, showing a complete workflow from drawing entry to plotted output.
message: A clear view of your next design.
Autodesk AutoCAD on Logix Artemis PRO. From drawing to plotted output.
See the drawing clearly
Native 800x600 drawing area on the 17-inch screen, four shades selected from 16 levels, static CAD palette and demonstrated line quality.
Keep commands and drawing in view
Colour command/status display alongside the dedicated drawing screen, with explicit keyboard/mouse focus.
Take the drawing beyond the screen
Save, reopen, exchange and plot the same test drawing; verify coordinates and output scale.
Buy an application with a supported platform
Autodesk application support and Logix hardware/integration support, qualified configurations, dealer training and a clear upgrade route.
Bring a drawing. See it on Artemis. Take home the plot.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify configurations and distinguish demonstrations from release commitments.

marketing_presentation.description: Do not promise 16 simultaneous shades at 800x600x2bpp.
Advertise 60 Hz only after the selected HD17H derivative is qualified.
No claim that a binary TTL/ECL amplifier becomes grayscale solely through a digital controller.
Present the release-quality Artemis build at COMDEX; commercial shipment remains conditional on acceptance and agreed Autodesk terms.

marketing_steps.description: Show the CAD workflow from drawing to plotted output.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Open a representative mechanical or floor-plan drawing from disk; show the command screen and drawing screen together.
Create and edit supported lines/arcs using typed coordinates and mouse input. Use only commands present in the qualified AutoCAD 1.0 build.
Pan/zoom and compare ordinary versus antialiased line rendering at the same scale. State measured redraw behaviour; do not promise arbitrary real-time performance.
